section_1.title: The Mystery of the Square Wave
section_1.content: Introduce a 'Musical Robot' named Oscillo who can only sing pure, smooth sine waves. Oscillo wants to mimic a harsh, blocky 'Square Wave' produced by a synthesizer. This sets the stage: how can smooth curves create sharp corners?
section_1.example: Oscillo the Robot tries to match a jagged 1Hz square wave using only rounded 'S' shaped motions.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Symmetry and Periodicity
section_2.content: Briefly review 'Odd Functions' (Symmetry around the origin). Explain that because a Square Wave is odd ($f(-x) = -f(x)$), we only need Pure Sine waves to describe it, skipping Cosines entirely. This simplifies our toolkit.
section_2.example: An animation showing a sine wave being flipped across both the X and Y axes to show it perfectly overlaps with itself, just like our Square Wave target.

section_3.title: The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)
section_3.content: Present the Pure Sine Series formula: $f(x) = \sum b_n \sin(n\omega x)$. Explain that 'n' represents the harmonic number. Visualizing 'n=1' as the base note and 'n=3, 5, 7...' as the overtones.
section_3.example: A graphic showing a guitar string vibrating as a whole (n=1), then in two halves (n=2), then three (n=3), each adding a higher pitch.

section_4.title: The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients
section_4.content: Explain $b_n$ using 'Graphical Overlap'. If we multiply our Square Wave by a specific Sine wave and the area under the resulting curve is large, that Sine wave is a 'strong ingredient'. This is the integral calculation visualized as a color-coded area.
section_4.example: An animation showing a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 1Hz Sine wave (mostly positive area = large $b_1$) vs. a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 2Hz Sine wave (positive and negative areas cancel out = $b_2$ is zero).

section_5.title: The Construction Site (Animation)
section_5.content: A fast-paced visual assembly. Start with the fundamental sine wave. Layer by layer, add the 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonics with decreasing amplitudes ($1/n$). Watch the 'wobbles' at the top of the wave flatten out into a straight line.
section_5.example: As each sine wave is added, the 'corners' of the sum get sharper, showing how infinite smooth waves eventually create a perfect sharp corner.

section_6.title: Real-World Application: Audio Compression
section_6.content: Conclude with why this matters. Instead of storing every point of a complex sound wave, a computer only needs to store the 'recipe' (the $b_n$ values). This is the secret behind MP3s and digital communication.
section_6.example: Oscillo the Robot sends a list of 5 numbers to a friend instead of a heavy recording; the friend uses the Fourier Series to 'rebuild' the sound perfectly.

outline.title: The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)
outline.content: Present the Pure Sine Series formula: $f(x) = \sum b_n \sin(n\omega x)$. Explain that 'n' represents the harmonic number. Visualizing 'n=1' as the base note and 'n=3, 5, 7...' as the overtones.
outline.example: A graphic showing a guitar string vibrating as a whole (n=1), then in two halves (n=2), then three (n=3), each adding a higher pitch.

storyboard.title: The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)
lecture_lines: The Fourier Series combines sines of different frequencies.
n=1 is the fundamental, the base pitch we hear.
Higher values of n represent overtones or harmonics.
Each harmonic adds detail and texture to the sound.
Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal.
animations: Display the Fourier series formula $\sum b_n \sin(n\omega x)$ in #FFFF00.
Highlight $n$ and label it "Harmonic Number" in #00FFFF.
Show a string vibrating at $n=1$ (Fundamental) in #D3D3D3.
Add vibrations for $n=3$ and $n=5$ (Overtones) in #FFA500.
Flash the higher $n$ values to emphasize their role as "detail".

outline.title: The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients
outline.content: Explain $b_n$ using 'Graphical Overlap'. If we multiply our Square Wave by a specific Sine wave and the area under the resulting curve is large, that Sine wave is a 'strong ingredient'. This is the integral calculation visualized as a color-coded area.
outline.example: An animation showing a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 1Hz Sine wave (mostly positive area = large $b_1$) vs. a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 2Hz Sine wave (positive and negative areas cancel out = $b_2$ is zero).

storyboard.title: The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients
lecture_lines: Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists.
We find them by multiplying the signal by sines.
Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient.
If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present.
This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave.
animations: Overlay a square wave (#FF0000) and sine wave (#00FF00).
Shade the overlap area yellow (#FFFF00) to represent the coefficient $b_n$.
Show a mismatching frequency where positive/negative areas cancel to zero.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset to the right side of the screen
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0 
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Real-World Application: Audio Compression"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Computers store these harmonic recipes instead of raw data.",
            "This \"shorthand\" allows for efficient digital audio compression.",
            "Fourier series turn complex sounds into simple, manageable lists."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lecture lines
        c1 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for recipe
        c2 = "#00FF00"  # Green for reconstruction
        c3 = "#FFFFFF"  # White for labels

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))

        # Recipe List: b1, b3, b5, b7, b9
        recipe_title = Text("Recipe [bn]", font_size=24, color=c1)
        self.place_at_grid(recipe_title, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bn_values = [
            MathTex("b_1 = 1.00", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_3 = 0.33", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_5 = 0.20", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_7 = 0.14", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_9 = 0.11", color=c1)
        ]
        recipe_list = VGroup(*bn_values).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(recipe_list, "C2", "E4", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Write(recipe_title))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Write(val) for val in bn_values], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(c2))

        # Create Axes for wave reconstruction
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            axis_config={"color": GREY},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)

        # Function for square wave reconstruction (5 harmonics)
        # 4/pi * sum sin(nx)/n for odd n
        def square_wave_recon(x):
            return (4/PI) * (
                np.sin(x) + 
                (1/3) * np.sin(3*x) + 
                (1/5) * np.sin(5*x) + 
                (1/7) * np.sin(7*x) + 
                (1/9) * np.sin(9*x)
            )

        wave_graph = axes.plot(square_wave_recon, color=c2)

        # Transform the recipe into the wave
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(recipe_list, wave_graph),
            FadeOut(recipe_title),
            Create(axes)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(c3))

        label_compression = Text("Audio Compression", font_size=24, color=c3)
        label_mp3 = Text("MP3 Standard", font_size=24, color=c3)

        self.place_at_grid(label_compression, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_mp3, "F5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Write(label_compression))
        self.play(Write(label_mp3))
        self.wait(2)

        )

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Construction Site"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- We start with the smooth, fundamental sine wave.",
            "- Adding the third harmonic begins to flatten the peaks.",
            "- The fifth and seventh harmonics sharpen the vertical edges.",
            "- As we add more, the 'wiggles' settle into blocks.",
            "- Infinite smooth waves eventually build perfect sharp corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_H3 = "#00FFFF"           # Cyan
        COLOR_H_ALL = "#FFFFFF"        # White

        # Axes setup (placed in area A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        self.add(axes)

        # Fourier summation function: f(x) = sum_{n=1,3,...}^N (1/n) * sin(nx)
        def fourier_sum(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/n) * np.sin(n * x) for n in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        
        current_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_H3)

        # Visualize the 3rd harmonic before summing

        h3_label = MathTex("n=3", color=COLOR_H3, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(h3_label, "B6")
        
        sum_wave_n3 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 3), color=COLOR_H3)
        
        self.play(Create(h3_wave), Write(h3_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(h3_wave),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        self.place_at_grid(n_label_7, "A6")

            FadeOut(n_label),

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists.",
            "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines.",
            "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient.",
            "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present.",
            "This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SQUARE = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_SINE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SQUARE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6")
        
        square_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1, color=COLOR_SQUARE, use_smoothing=False)
        
        self.play(Write(axes))
        self.play(Create(square_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        sine_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        
        self.play(Create(sine_wave_n1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        # For n=1, product is |sin(x)|
        product_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: abs(np.sin(x)), color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_fill_n1 = axes.get_area(product_wave_n1, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color=COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.3)
        
        label_b1 = MathTex("b_1 = \\text{Large Value}", color=COLOR_AREA, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b1, "A3")

        self.play(FadeOut(square_wave), FadeOut(sine_wave_n1))
        self.play(Create(product_wave_n1), FadeIn(area_fill_n1), Write(label_b1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_AREA)

        sine_wave_n2 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        
        # Product for n=2: square(x) * sin(2x)
        # sin(2x) has two periods in 0..2pi. 
        # 0..pi: square=1, product=sin(2x). One full cycle. Area = 0.
        # pi..2pi: square=-1, product=-sin(2x). One full cycle. Area = 0.

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)

                x = 0.5 + j * 1

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists.",
            "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines.",
            "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient.",
            "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present.",

        ]

        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        # For n=1, product is |sin(x)|
        product_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: abs(np.sin(x)), color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_fill_n1 = axes.get_area(product_wave_n1, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color=COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.3)
        
        label_b1 = MathTex("b_1 = \\text{Large Value}", color=COLOR_AREA, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b1, "A3")

        self.play(FadeOut(square_wave), FadeOut(sine_wave_n1))
        self.play(Create(product_wave_n1), FadeIn(area_fill_n1), Write(label_b1))

        # "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_AREA)

        # Product for n=2: square(x) * sin(2x)

        # pi..2pi: square=-1, product=-sin(2x). Area = 0.

        self.place_at_grid(label_b2, "A3")

            FadeOut(product_wave_n1), 
            FadeOut(area_fill_n1), 
            FadeOut(label_b1)
        )
        self.play(Create(square_wave_again), Create(sine_wave_n2))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(square_wave_again),
            FadeOut(sine_wave_n2),
            Create(product_wave_n2),
            FadeIn(area_fill_n2),
            Write(label_b2)
        )

        # "This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Final Summary Formula
        final_formula = MathTex("b_n = \\frac{1}{\\pi} \\int_0^{2\\pi} f(t) \\sin(nt) dt", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(final_formula, "C3")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(product_wave_n2), FadeOut(area_fill_n2), FadeOut(label_b2))
        self.play(Write(final_formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)", [
            "The Fourier Series combines sines of different frequencies.",
            "n=1 is the fundamental, the base pitch we hear.",
            "Higher values of n represent overtones or harmonics.",
            "Each harmonic adds detail and texture to the sound.",
            "Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_L1 = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_L2 = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_L3 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_L4 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_L5 = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#D3D3D3"
        COLOR_OVERTONE = "#FFA500"

        # Time Tracker for animations
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        self.add(time_tracker)
        time_tracker.add_updater(lambda t, dt: t.increment_value(dt))

        # Helper function for vibrating strings
        def get_string(n, color, length=4, amplitude=0.4):
            res = 50
            points = [np.array([x, 0, 0]) for x in np.linspace(-length/2, length/2, res)]
            mobj = VMobject(color=color).set_points_as_corners(points)
            mobj.n_val = n
            mobj.amp = amplitude
            mobj.len = length
            mobj.base_center = np.array([0,0,0])
            
            def string_updater(m):
                t = time_tracker.get_value()
                new_points = []
                for x_rel in np.linspace(-m.len/2, m.len/2, res):
                    y = m.amp * np.sin(m.n_val * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(m.n_val * t * 4)
                    new_points.append(m.base_center + np.array([x_rel, y, 0]))
                m.set_points_as_corners(new_points)
            
            mobj.add_updater(string_updater)
            return mobj

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        formula = MathTex(r"\sum b_n \sin(n \omega x)", color=COLOR_L1)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        n_label = Text("Harmonic Number", font_size=20, color=COLOR_L2)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        string_n1 = get_string(1, COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL, length=4.5)
        self.place_in_area(string_n1, "C1", "C6")
        string_n1.base_center = string_n1.get_center()
        
        label_n1 = Text("n=1 (Fundamental)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n1, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_L2))
        self.play(
            formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("n", COLOR_L2),
            Write(n_label),
            Create(string_n1),
            Write(label_n1)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Add vibrations for n=3 and n=5 (Overtones) in #FFA500.
        
        string_n3 = get_string(3, COLOR_OVERTONE, length=4.5, amplitude=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(string_n3, "D1", "D6")
        string_n3.base_center = string_n3.get_center()
        
        label_n3 = Text("n=3", font_size=18, color=COLOR_OVERTONE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n3, "D1", scale_factor=0.8)

        string_n5 = get_string(5, COLOR_OVERTONE, length=4.5, amplitude=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(string_n5, "E1", "E6")
        string_n5.base_center = string_n5.get_center()
        
        label_n5 = Text("n=5", font_size=18, color=COLOR_OVERTONE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n5, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_L3))
        self.play(
            Create(string_n3),
            Write(label_n3),
            Create(string_n5),
            Write(label_n5)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Flash the higher n values to emphasize their role as "detail".
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_L4))
        self.play(
            Flash(string_n3, color=COLOR_OVERTONE, flash_radius=2, line_stroke_width=3),
            Flash(string_n5, color=COLOR_OVERTONE, flash_radius=2, line_stroke_width=3),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal.
        # Showing the sum of harmonics as a "Blueprint" string.

        )

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Construction Site"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- We start with the smooth, fundamental sine wave.",
            "- Adding the third harmonic begins to flatten the peaks.",
            "- The fifth and seventh harmonics sharpen the vertical edges.",
            "- As we add more, the 'wiggles' settle into blocks.",
            "- Infinite smooth waves eventually build perfect sharp corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_H3 = "#00FFFF"           # Cyan
        COLOR_H_ALL = "#FFFFFF"        # White

        # Axes setup (placed in area A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        self.add(axes)

        # Fourier summation function: f(x) = sum_{n=1,3,...}^N (1/n) * sin(nx)
        def fourier_sum(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/n) * np.sin(n * x) for n in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        
        current_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        n_label = MathTex("n=1", color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "A6")

        self.play(Create(current_wave), Write(n_label), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_H3)

        # Visualize the 3rd harmonic before summing
        h3_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: (1/3) * np.sin(3*x), color=COLOR_H3)
        h3_label = MathTex("n=3", color=COLOR_H3, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(h3_label, "B6")
        
        sum_wave_n3 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 3), color=COLOR_H3)
        
        self.play(Create(h3_wave), Write(h3_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(h3_wave),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        # Advance to 7 harmonics
        sum_wave_n7 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 7), color=COLOR_H_ALL)
        n_label_7 = MathTex("n=1...7", color=COLOR_H_ALL, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label_7, "A6")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(n_label),
            FadeOut(h3_label),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n7),
            Write(n_label_7),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        # Rapidly add harmonics to approach a square wave
        n_steps = [11, 15, 21, 31, 51]
        for n_val in n_steps:
            next_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, n_val), color=COLOR_H_ALL)
            self.play(Transform(current_wave, next_wave), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW) # Using Yellow for emphasis on "corners"

        # Highlight corners to emphasize sharpness
        corner_highlight_1 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.coords_to_point(PI/2, 0.8))
        corner_highlight_2 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.coords_to_point(-PI/2, -0.8))
        
        sharp_text = Text("Sharp Corners", color=YELLOW, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(sharp_text, "D6")

        self.play(
            Create(corner_highlight_1), 
            Create(corner_highlight_2), 
            Write(sharp_text),
            run_time=2

I have generated the Manim code for `section_5` of the "The Building Blocks of Sound: Pure Fourier Sine Series" video.

### Key Implementation Details:
- **Visual Anchor System**: The entire animation is confined to the right-side 6x6 grid (A1-F6).
- **Matching Colors**: Each lecture line color-matches its visual counterpart:
    - Fundamental wave and Line 1 use **Green** (#00FF00).
    - 3rd harmonic and Line 2 use **Cyan** (#00FFFF).
    - Higher harmonics and Lines 3-4 use **White** (#FFFFFF).
    - Sharp corners highlight and Line 5 use **Yellow** (#FFFF00).
- **Fourier Summation**: The code implements a summation function $f(x) = \sum_{n=1,3...}^N \frac{1}{n} \sin(nx)$ to visually build a square-like wave.
- **Performance**: Used `Transform` for efficient state-to-state animations instead of computationally heavy updaters, ensuring the section renders within the timeout limits.

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Construction Site"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- We start with the smooth, fundamental sine wave.",
            "- Adding the third harmonic begins to flatten the peaks.",
            "- The fifth and seventh harmonics sharpen the vertical edges.",
            "- As we add more, the 'wiggles' settle into blocks.",
            "- Infinite smooth waves eventually build perfect sharp corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_H3 = "#00FFFF"           # Cyan
        COLOR_H_ALL = "#FFFFFF"        # White

        # Axes setup (placed in area A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        self.add(axes)

        # Fourier summation function: f(x) = sum_{n=1,3,...}^N (1/n) * sin(nx)
        def fourier_sum(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/n) * np.sin(n * x) for n in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        
        current_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        n_label = MathTex("n=1", color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "A6")

        self.play(Create(current_wave), Write(n_label), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_H3)

        # Visualize the 3rd harmonic before summing
        h3_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: (1/3) * np.sin(3*x), color=COLOR_H3)
        h3_label = MathTex("n=3", color=COLOR_H3, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(h3_label, "B6")
        
        sum_wave_n3 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 3), color=COLOR_H3)
        
        self.play(Create(h3_wave), Write(h3_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(h3_wave),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        # Advance to 7 harmonics
        sum_wave_n7 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 7), color=COLOR_H_ALL)
        n_label_7 = MathTex("n=1...7", color=COLOR_H_ALL, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label_7, "A6")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(n_label),
            FadeOut(h3_label),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n7),
            Write(n_label_7),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        # Rapidly add harmonics to approach a square wave
        n_steps = [11, 15, 21, 31, 51]
        for n_val in n_steps:
            next_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, n_val), color=COLOR_H_ALL)
            self.play(Transform(current_wave, next_wave), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW) # Using Yellow for emphasis on "corners"

        # Highlight corners to emphasize sharpness
        corner_highlight_1 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.coords_to_point(PI/2, 0.8))
        corner_highlight_2 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.coords_to_point(-PI/2, -0.8))
        
        sharp_text = Text("Sharp Corners", color=YELLOW, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(sharp_text, "D6")

        self.play(
            Create(corner_highlight_1), 
            Create(corner_highlight_2), 
            Write(sharp_text),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)
```

section_1.title: The Mystery of the Square Wave
section_1.content: Introduce a 'Musical Robot' named Oscillo who can only sing pure, smooth sine waves. Oscillo wants to mimic a harsh, blocky 'Square Wave' produced by a synthesizer. This sets the stage: how can smooth curves create sharp corners?
section_1.example: Oscillo the Robot tries to match a jagged 1Hz square wave using only rounded 'S' shaped motions.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Symmetry and Periodicity
section_2.content: Briefly review 'Odd Functions' (Symmetry around the origin). Explain that because a Square Wave is odd ($f(-x) = -f(x)$), we only need Pure Sine waves to describe it, skipping Cosines entirely. This simplifies our toolkit.
section_2.example: An animation showing a sine wave being flipped across both the X and Y axes to show it perfectly overlaps with itself, just like our Square Wave target.

section_3.title: The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)
section_3.content: Present the Pure Sine Series formula: $f(x) = \sum b_n \sin(n\omega x)$. Explain that 'n' represents the harmonic number. Visualizing 'n=1' as the base note and 'n=3, 5, 7...' as the overtones.
section_3.example: A graphic showing a guitar string vibrating as a whole (n=1), then in two halves (n=2), then three (n=3), each adding a higher pitch.

section_4.title: The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients

section_4.example: An animation showing a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 1Hz Sine wave (mostly positive area = large $b_1$) vs. a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 2Hz Sine wave (positive and negative areas cancel out = $b_2$ is zero).

section_6.content: Conclude with why this matters. Instead of storing every point of a complex sound wave, a computer only needs to store the 'recipe' (the $b_n$ values). This is the secret behind MP3s and digital communication.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mystery of the Square Wave", [
            "Meet Oscillo, a robot who sings smooth sine waves.",
            "He wants to mimic this jagged square wave synthesizer.",
            "Can smooth curves ever create such sharp, blocky corners?"
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Robot Oscillo (#ADD8E6)
        body = RoundedRectangle(width=1, height=1.2, corner_radius=0.1, color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.5)
        head = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(body, UP, buff=0.05)
        eye_l = Circle(radius=0.05, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(head.get_center() + LEFT * 0.15 + UP * 0.05)
        eye_r = Circle(radius=0.05, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(head.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.15 + UP * 0.05)
        mouth = Arc(radius=0.15, start_angle=PI, angle=PI, color=WHITE).move_to(head.get_center() + DOWN * 0.1)
        oscillo = VGroup(body, head, eye_l, eye_r, mouth)
        self.place_at_grid(oscillo, "C1", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Smooth sine wave (#00FF00)
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[0, 2], color="#00FF00")
        # Shift sine wave points to center it roughly before scaling
        sine_wave.shift(LEFT * 1)
        self.place_in_area(sine_wave, "B3", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        self.play(FadeIn(oscillo), Create(sine_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Square wave (#FF0000) labeled "Target"
        # Manual corners for sharp square wave
        sq_points = [
            [0, 1, 0], [0.5, 1, 0], [0.5, -1, 0], 
            [1, -1, 0], [1, 1, 0], [1.5, 1, 0], 
            [1.5, -1, 0], [2, -1, 0]
        ]
        # Shift points so center is at origin before placing
        sq_points = [[p[0]-1, p[1], p[2]] for p in sq_points]
        square_wave = VMobject(color="#FF0000").set_points_as_corners([np.array(p) for p in sq_points])
        
        self.place_in_area(square_wave, "B3", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        target_label = Text("Target", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(target_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(sine_wave),
            FadeIn(square_wave),
            FadeIn(target_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Oscillo oscillates between the smooth and sharp waves with confusion.
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, "A1", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            oscillo.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.1),
            FadeIn(question_mark)
        )
        
        # Shake Oscillo (confusion)
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(oscillo.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.1)
            self.play(oscillo.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.1)
        
        self.play(Indicate(square_wave, color="#FF0000"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Prerequisite: Symmetry and Periodicity"
        lines = [
            "Square waves are odd functions, symmetric around the origin.",
            "This symmetry means we only need pure sine waves.",
            "No cosines are required, simplifying our mathematical toolkit."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        SINE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        SQUARE_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        AXES_COLOR = BLUE_D
        LABEL_COLOR = YELLOW_A
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Square waves are odd functions, symmetric around the origin.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(SINE_COLOR)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": AXES_COLOR, "include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        origin_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(0, 0, 0), color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        sine_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=SINE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(origin_dot))
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # This symmetry means we only need pure sine waves.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SINE_COLOR)
        
        # Ghost sine to show the starting position during rotation
        ghost_sine = sine_wave.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        self.add(ghost_sine)
        
        # Rotate 180 degrees to demonstrate odd symmetry f(-x) = -f(x)
        self.play(
            Rotate(sine_wave, angle=PI, about_point=axes.c2p(0, 0, 0)),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        odd_math = MathTex("f(-x) = -f(x)", color=LABEL_COLOR, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(odd_math, "F4")
        self.play(Write(odd_math))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # No cosines are required, simplifying our mathematical toolkit.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(SQUARE_COLOR)
        
        # Transformation to Square Wave
        # Square wave: 4/pi * sum(sin(n*x)/n) for odd n
        # For this demonstration, the simple signum of sine is enough
        square_wave = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1 if np.sin(x) < 0 else 0,
            color=SQUARE_COLOR,
            use_smoothing=False
        )
        
        sine_only_text = Text("Sine-Only Series", color=SQUARE_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(sine_only_text, "F4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(sine_wave),
            FadeOut(ghost_sine),
            ReplacementTransform(odd_math, sine_only_text),
            Create(square_wave)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final rotation to show square wave also has the same property
        self.play(
            Rotate(square_wave, angle=PI, about_point=axes.c2p(0, 0, 0)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)", [
            "The Fourier Series combines sines of different frequencies.",
            "n=1 is the fundamental, the base pitch we hear.",
            "Higher values of n represent overtones or harmonics.",
            "Each harmonic adds detail and texture to the sound.",
            "Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_L1 = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_L2 = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_L3 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_L4 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_L5 = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#D3D3D3"
        COLOR_OVERTONE = "#FFA500"

        # Time Tracker for animations
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        self.add(time_tracker)
        time_tracker.add_updater(lambda t, dt: t.increment_value(dt))

        # Helper function for vibrating strings
        def get_string(n, color, length=4, amplitude=0.4):
            res = 50
            points = [np.array([x, 0, 0]) for x in np.linspace(-length/2, length/2, res)]
            mobj = VMobject(color=color).set_points_as_corners(points)
            mobj.n_val = n
            mobj.amp = amplitude
            mobj.len = length
            mobj.base_center = np.array([0,0,0])
            
            def string_updater(m):
                t = time_tracker.get_value()
                new_points = []
                for x_rel in np.linspace(-m.len/2, m.len/2, res):
                    y = m.amp * np.sin(m.n_val * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(m.n_val * t * 4)
                    new_points.append(m.base_center + np.array([x_rel, y, 0]))
                m.set_points_as_corners(new_points)
            
            mobj.add_updater(string_updater)
            return mobj

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the Fourier series formula \sum b_n \sin(n \omega x) in #FFFF00
        formula = MathTex(r"\sum b_n \sin(n \omega x)", color=COLOR_L1)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_L1))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight n and label it "Harmonic Number" in #00FFFF.
        # Show a string vibrating at n=1 (Fundamental) in #D3D3D3.
        
        n_label = Text("Harmonic Number", font_size=20, color=COLOR_L2)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        string_n1 = get_string(1, COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL, length=4.5)
        self.place_in_area(string_n1, "C1", "C6")
        string_n1.base_center = string_n1.get_center()
        
        label_n1 = Text("n=1 (Fundamental)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n1, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_L2))
        self.play(
            formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("n", COLOR_L2),
            Write(n_label),
            Create(string_n1),
            Write(label_n1)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Add vibrations for n=3 and n=5 (Overtones) in #FFA500.
        
        string_n3 = get_string(3, COLOR_OVERTONE, length=4.5, amplitude=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(string_n3, "D1", "D6")
        string_n3.base_center = string_n3.get_center()
        
        label_n3 = Text("n=3", font_size=18, color=COLOR_OVERTONE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n3, "D1", scale_factor=0.8)

        string_n5 = get_string(5, COLOR_OVERTONE, length=4.5, amplitude=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(string_n5, "E1", "E6")
        string_n5.base_center = string_n5.get_center()
        
        label_n5 = Text("n=5", font_size=18, color=COLOR_OVERTONE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n5, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_L3))
        self.play(
            Create(string_n3),
            Write(label_n3),
            Create(string_n5),
            Write(label_n5)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Flash the higher n values to emphasize their role as "detail".
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_L4))
        self.play(
            Flash(string_n3, color=COLOR_OVERTONE, flash_radius=2, line_stroke_width=3),
            Flash(string_n5, color=COLOR_OVERTONE, flash_radius=2, line_stroke_width=3),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal.
        # Showing the sum of harmonics as a "Blueprint" string.
        
        blueprint_string = get_string(1, COLOR_L5, length=4.5)
        def blueprint_updater(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            res = 50
            new_points = []
            for x_rel in np.linspace(-m.len/2, m.len/2, res):
                # Harmonic superposition: b1*sin(1x) + b3*sin(3x) + b5*sin(5x)
                y1 = 0.5 * np.sin(1 * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(1 * t * 4)
                y3 = 0.15 * np.sin(3 * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(3 * t * 4)
                y5 = 0.08 * np.sin(5 * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(5 * t * 4)
                y = y1 + y3 + y5
                new_points.append(m.base_center + np.array([x_rel, y, 0]))
            m.set_points_as_corners(new_points)

        # Update the default updater with the composite one
        blueprint_string.remove_updater(blueprint_string.updaters[0])
        blueprint_string.add_updater(blueprint_updater)
        
        self.place_in_area(blueprint_string, "F1", "F6")
        blueprint_string.base_center = blueprint_string.get_center()
        
        label_blueprint = Text("Complete Blueprint (Sum)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_blueprint, "F1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_L5))
        self.play(
            Create(blueprint_string),
            Write(label_blueprint)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists.",
            "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines.",
            "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient.",
            "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present.",
            "This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SQUARE = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_SINE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SQUARE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6")
        
        square_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1, color=COLOR_SQUARE, use_smoothing=False)
        
        self.play(Write(axes))
        self.play(Create(square_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        sine_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        
        self.play(Create(sine_wave_n1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        # For n=1, product is |sin(x)|
        product_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: abs(np.sin(x)), color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_fill_n1 = axes.get_area(product_wave_n1, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color=COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.3)
        
        label_b1 = MathTex("b_1 = \\text{Large Value}", color=COLOR_AREA, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b1, "A3")

        self.play(FadeOut(square_wave), FadeOut(sine_wave_n1))
        self.play(Create(product_wave_n1), FadeIn(area_fill_n1), Write(label_b1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        # Return to Square and show Sine n=2
        square_wave_again = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1, color=COLOR_SQUARE, use_smoothing=False)
        sine_wave_n2 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        
        # Product for n=2: square(x) * sin(2x)
        # sin(2x) has two periods in 0..2pi. 
        # 0..pi: square=1, product=sin(2x). One full cycle. Area = 0.
        # pi..2pi: square=-1, product=-sin(2x). One full cycle. Area = 0.
        product_wave_n2 = axes.plot(lambda x: (1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1) * np.sin(2 * x), color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_fill_n2 = axes.get_area(product_wave_n2, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color=COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.3)

        label_b2 = MathTex("b_2 = 0", color=COLOR_AREA, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b2, "A3")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(product_wave_n1), 
            FadeOut(area_fill_n1), 
            FadeOut(label_b1)
        )
        self.play(Create(square_wave_again), Create(sine_wave_n2))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(square_wave_again),
            FadeOut(sine_wave_n2),
            Create(product_wave_n2),
            FadeIn(area_fill_n2),
            Write(label_b2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Final Summary
        final_formula = MathTex("b_n = \\frac{1}{\\pi} \\int_0^{2\\pi} f(t) \\sin(nt) dt", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(final_formula, "C3")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(product_wave_n2), FadeOut(area_fill_n2), FadeOut(label_b2))
        self.play(Write(final_formula))
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Construction Site"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- We start with the smooth, fundamental sine wave.",
            "- Adding the third harmonic begins to flatten the peaks.",
            "- The fifth and seventh harmonics sharpen the vertical edges.",
            "- As we add more, the 'wiggles' settle into blocks.",
            "- Infinite smooth waves eventually build perfect sharp corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_H3 = "#00FFFF"           # Cyan
        COLOR_H_ALL = "#FFFFFF"        # White

        # Axes setup (placed in area A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        self.add(axes)

        # Fourier summation function: f(x) = sum_{n=1,3,...}^N (1/n) * sin(nx)
        def fourier_sum(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/n) * np.sin(n * x) for n in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        
        current_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        n_label = MathTex("n=1", color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "A6")

        self.play(Create(current_wave), Write(n_label), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_H3)

        # Visualize the 3rd harmonic before summing
        h3_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: (1/3) * np.sin(3*x), color=COLOR_H3)
        h3_label = MathTex("n=3", color=COLOR_H3, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(h3_label, "B6")
        
        sum_wave_n3 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 3), color=COLOR_H3)
        
        self.play(Create(h3_wave), Write(h3_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(h3_wave),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        # Advance to 7 harmonics
        sum_wave_n7 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 7), color=COLOR_H_ALL)
        n_label_7 = MathTex("n=1...7", color=COLOR_H_ALL, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label_7, "A6")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(n_label),
            FadeOut(h3_label),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n7),
            Write(n_label_7),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_H_ALL)

        # Rapidly add harmonics to approach a square wave
        n_steps = [11, 15, 21, 31, 51]
        for n_val in n_steps:
            next_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, n_val), color=COLOR_H_ALL)
            self.play(Transform(current_wave, next_wave), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW) # Using Yellow for emphasis on "corners"

        # Highlight corners to emphasize sharpness
        corner_highlight_1 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.coords_to_point(PI/2, 0.8))
        corner_highlight_2 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.coords_to_point(-PI/2, -0.8))
        
        sharp_text = Text("Sharp Corners", color=YELLOW, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(sharp_text, "D6")

        self.play(
            Create(corner_highlight_1), 
            Create(corner_highlight_2), 
            Write(sharp_text),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Real-World Application: Audio Compression"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Computers store these harmonic recipes instead of raw data.",
            "This \"shorthand\" allows for efficient digital audio compression.",
            "Fourier series turn complex sounds into simple, manageable lists."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lecture lines
        c1 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for recipe
        c2 = "#00FF00"  # Green for reconstruction
        c3 = "#FFFFFF"  # White for labels

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))

        # Recipe List: b1, b3, b5, b7, b9
        recipe_title = Text("Recipe [bn]", font_size=24, color=c1)
        self.place_at_grid(recipe_title, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bn_values = [
            MathTex("b_1 = 1.00", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_3 = 0.33", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_5 = 0.20", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_7 = 0.14", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_9 = 0.11", color=c1)
        ]
        recipe_list = VGroup(*bn_values).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(recipe_list, "C2", "E4", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Write(recipe_title))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Write(val) for val in bn_values], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(c2))

        # Create Axes for wave reconstruction
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            axis_config={"color": GREY},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)

        # Function for square wave reconstruction (5 harmonics)
        # 4/pi * sum sin(nx)/n for odd n
        def square_wave_recon(x):
            return (4/PI) * (
                np.sin(x) + 
                (1/3) * np.sin(3*x) + 
                (1/5) * np.sin(5*x) + 
                (1/7) * np.sin(7*x) + 
                (1/9) * np.sin(9*x)
            )

        wave_graph = axes.plot(square_wave_recon, color=c2)

        # Transform the recipe into the wave
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(recipe_list, wave_graph),
            FadeOut(recipe_title),
            Create(axes)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(c3))

        label_compression = Text("Audio Compression", font_size=24, color=c3)
        label_mp3 = Text("MP3 Standard", font_size=24, color=c3)

        self.place_at_grid(label_compression, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_mp3, "F5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Write(label_compression))
        self.play(Write(label_mp3))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)
outline.content: Present the Pure Sine Series formula: $f(x) = \sum b_n \sin(n\omega x)$. Explain that 'n' represents the harmonic number. Visualizing 'n=1' as the base note and 'n=3, 5, 7...' as the overtones.
outline.example: A graphic showing a guitar string vibrating as a whole (n=1), then in two halves (n=2), then three (n=3), each adding a higher pitch.

storyboard.title: The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)
lecture_lines: The Fourier Series combines sines of different frequencies.
n=1 is the fundamental, the base pitch we hear.
Higher values of n represent overtones or harmonics.
Each harmonic adds detail and texture to the sound.
Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal.
animations: Display the Fourier series formula $\sum b_n \sin(n\omega x)$ in #FFFF00.
Highlight $n$ and label it "Harmonic Number" in #00FFFF.
Show a string vibrating at $n=1$ (Fundamental) in #D3D3D3.
Add vibrations for $n=3$ and $n=5$ (Overtones) in #FFA500.
Flash the higher $n$ values to emphasize their role as "detail".

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Harmonic Blueprint (The Formula)", [
            "The Fourier Series combines sines of different frequencies.",
            "n=1 is the fundamental, the base pitch we hear.",
            "Higher values of n represent overtones or harmonics.",
            "Each harmonic adds detail and texture to the sound.",
            "Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_L1 = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_L2 = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_L3 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_L4 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_L5 = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL = "#D3D3D3"
        COLOR_OVERTONE = "#FFA500"

        # Time Tracker for animations
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        self.add(time_tracker)
        time_tracker.add_updater(lambda t, dt: t.increment_value(dt))

        # Helper function for vibrating strings
        def get_string(n, color, length=4, amplitude=0.4):
            res = 50
            points = [np.array([x, 0, 0]) for x in np.linspace(-length/2, length/2, res)]
            mobj = VMobject(color=color).set_points_as_corners(points)
            mobj.n_val = n
            mobj.amp = amplitude
            mobj.len = length
            mobj.base_center = np.array([0,0,0])
            
            def string_updater(m):
                t = time_tracker.get_value()
                new_points = []
                for x_rel in np.linspace(-m.len/2, m.len/2, res):
                    y = m.amp * np.sin(m.n_val * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(m.n_val * t * 4)
                    new_points.append(m.base_center + np.array([x_rel, y, 0]))
                m.set_points_as_corners(new_points)
            
            mobj.add_updater(string_updater)
            return mobj

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the Fourier series formula \sum b_n \sin(n \omega x) in #FFFF00
        formula = MathTex(r"\sum b_n \sin(n \omega x)", color=COLOR_L1)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_L1))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight n and label it "Harmonic Number" in #00FFFF.
        # Show a string vibrating at n=1 (Fundamental) in #D3D3D3.
        
        n_label = Text("Harmonic Number", font_size=20, color=COLOR_L2)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        string_n1 = get_string(1, COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL, length=4.5)
        self.place_in_area(string_n1, "C1", "C6")
        string_n1.base_center = string_n1.get_center()
        
        label_n1 = Text("n=1 (Fundamental)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_FUNDAMENTAL)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n1, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_L2))
        self.play(
            formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("n", COLOR_L2),
            Write(n_label),
            Create(string_n1),
            Write(label_n1)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Add vibrations for n=3 and n=5 (Overtones) in #FFA500.
        
        string_n3 = get_string(3, COLOR_OVERTONE, length=4.5, amplitude=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(string_n3, "D1", "D6")
        string_n3.base_center = string_n3.get_center()
        
        label_n3 = Text("n=3", font_size=18, color=COLOR_OVERTONE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n3, "D1", scale_factor=0.8)

        string_n5 = get_string(5, COLOR_OVERTONE, length=4.5, amplitude=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(string_n5, "E1", "E6")
        string_n5.base_center = string_n5.get_center()
        
        label_n5 = Text("n=5", font_size=18, color=COLOR_OVERTONE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n5, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_L3))
        self.play(
            Create(string_n3),
            Write(label_n3),
            Create(string_n5),
            Write(label_n5)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Flash the higher n values to emphasize their role as "detail".
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_L4))
        self.play(
            Flash(string_n3, color=COLOR_OVERTONE, flash_radius=2, line_stroke_width=3),
            Flash(string_n5, color=COLOR_OVERTONE, flash_radius=2, line_stroke_width=3),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Together, they form the complete blueprint for any signal.
        # Showing the sum of harmonics as a "Blueprint" string.
        
        blueprint_string = get_string(1, COLOR_L5, length=4.5)
        def blueprint_updater(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            res = 50
            new_points = []
            for x_rel in np.linspace(-m.len/2, m.len/2, res):
                # Harmonic superposition: b1*sin(1x) + b3*sin(3x) + b5*sin(5x)
                y1 = 0.5 * np.sin(1 * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(1 * t * 4)
                y3 = 0.15 * np.sin(3 * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(3 * t * 4)
                y5 = 0.08 * np.sin(5 * PI * (x_rel + m.len/2) / m.len) * np.cos(5 * t * 4)
                y = y1 + y3 + y5
                new_points.append(m.base_center + np.array([x_rel, y, 0]))
            m.set_points_as_corners(new_points)

        # Update the default updater with the composite one
        blueprint_string.remove_updater(blueprint_string.updaters[0])
        blueprint_string.add_updater(blueprint_updater)
        
        self.place_in_area(blueprint_string, "F1", "F6")
        blueprint_string.base_center = blueprint_string.get_center()
        
        label_blueprint = Text("Complete Blueprint (Sum)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_blueprint, "F1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_L5))
        self.play(
            Create(blueprint_string),
            Write(label_blueprint)
        )
        self.wait(3)

storyboard.title: The Construction Site (Animation)

Adding the third harmonic begins to flatten the peaks.
The fifth and seventh harmonics sharpen the vertical edges.
As we add more, the 'wiggles' settle into blocks.
Infinite smooth waves eventually build perfect sharp corners.

Highlight the corners becoming sharper as more harmonics are added.

        self.add(axes)

        def fourier_sum(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/n) * np.sin(n * x) for n in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        sum_wave_n3 = axes.plot(lambda x: fourier_sum(x, 3), color=COLOR_H3)
        
        self.play(Create(h3_wave), Write(h3_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(h3_wave),
            Transform(current_wave, sum_wave_n3),

        )
        self.wait(1)

outline.content: Explain $b_n$ using 'Graphical Overlap'. If we multiply our Square Wave by a specific Sine wave and the area under the resulting curve is large, that Sine wave is a 'strong ingredient'. This is the integral calculation visualized as a color-coded area.
outline.example: An animation showing a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 1Hz Sine wave (mostly positive area = large $b_1$) vs. a 1Hz Square wave multiplied by a 2Hz Sine wave (positive and negative areas cancel out = $b_2$ is zero).

storyboard.title: The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients
lecture_lines: Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists.
We find them by multiplying the signal by sines.
Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient.
If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present.
This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave.

class TeachingScene(Scene):

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists.",
            "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines.",
            "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient.",
            "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present.",
            "This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Projection Trick: Calculating Coefficients", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SQUARE = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_SINE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Coefficients bn determine how much of each sine exists."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SQUARE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6")
        
        square_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1, color=COLOR_SQUARE, use_smoothing=False)
        
        self.play(Write(axes))
        self.play(Create(square_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We find them by multiplying the signal by sines."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        sine_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        
        self.play(Create(sine_wave_n1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Large overlap area means the sine is a strong ingredient."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        # For n=1, product is |sin(x)|
        product_wave_n1 = axes.plot(lambda x: abs(np.sin(x)), color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_fill_n1 = axes.get_area(product_wave_n1, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color=COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.3)
        
        label_b1 = MathTex("b_1 = \\text{Large Value}", color=COLOR_AREA, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b1, "A3")

        self.play(FadeOut(square_wave), FadeOut(sine_wave_n1))
        self.play(Create(product_wave_n1), FadeIn(area_fill_n1), Write(label_b1))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "If areas cancel out, that harmonic is not present."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_AREA)
        
        # Return to Square and show Sine n=2
        square_wave_again = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1, color=COLOR_SQUARE, use_smoothing=False)
        sine_wave_n2 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        
        # Product for n=2: square(x) * sin(2x)
        # sin(2x) has two periods in 0..2pi. 
        # 0..pi: square=1, product=sin(2x). One full cycle. Area = 0.
        # pi..2pi: square=-1, product=-sin(2x). One full cycle. Area = 0.
        product_wave_n2 = axes.plot(lambda x: (1 if np.sin(x) > 0 else -1) * np.sin(2 * x), color=COLOR_AREA)
        area_fill_n2 = axes.get_area(product_wave_n2, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color=COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.3)

        label_b2 = MathTex("b_2 = 0", color=COLOR_AREA, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b2, "A3")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(product_wave_n1), 
            FadeOut(area_fill_n1), 
            FadeOut(label_b1)
        )
        self.play(Create(square_wave_again), Create(sine_wave_n2))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(square_wave_again),
            FadeOut(sine_wave_n2),
            Create(product_wave_n2),
            FadeIn(area_fill_n2),
            Write(label_b2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This projection extracts the specific recipe for our wave."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Final Summary
        final_formula = MathTex("b_n = \\frac{1}{\\pi} \\int_0^{2\\pi} f(t) \\sin(nt) dt", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(final_formula, "C3")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(product_wave_n2), FadeOut(area_fill_n2), FadeOut(label_b2))
        self.play(Write(final_formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Real-World Application: Audio Compression"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Computers store these harmonic recipes instead of raw data.",
            "This \"shorthand\" allows for efficient digital audio compression.",
            "Fourier series turn complex sounds into simple, manageable lists."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lecture lines
        c1 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for recipe
        c2 = "#00FF00"  # Green for reconstruction
        c3 = "#FFFFFF"  # White for labels

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))

        # Recipe List: b1, b3, b5, b7, b9
        recipe_title = Text("Recipe [bn]", font_size=24, color=c1)
        self.place_at_grid(recipe_title, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bn_values = [
            MathTex("b_1 = 1.00", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_3 = 0.33", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_5 = 0.20", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_7 = 0.14", color=c1),
            MathTex("b_9 = 0.11", color=c1)
        ]
        recipe_list = VGroup(*bn_values).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(recipe_list, "C2", "E4", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Write(recipe_title))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Write(val) for val in bn_values], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(c2))

        # Create Axes for wave reconstruction
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            axis_config={"color": GREY},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)

        # Function for square wave reconstruction (5 harmonics)
        # 4/pi * sum sin(nx)/n for odd n
        def square_wave_recon(x):
            return (4/PI) * (
                np.sin(x) + 
                (1/3) * np.sin(3*x) + 
                (1/5) * np.sin(5*x) + 
                (1/7) * np.sin(7*x) + 
                (1/9) * np.sin(9*x)
            )

        wave_graph = axes.plot(square_wave_recon, color=c2)

        # Transform the recipe into the wave
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(recipe_list, wave_graph),
            FadeOut(recipe_title),
            Create(axes)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(c3))

        label_compression = Text("Audio Compression", font_size=24, color=c3)
        label_mp3 = Text("MP3 Standard", font_size=24, color=c3)

        self.place_at_grid(label_compression, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_mp3, "F5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Write(label_compression))
        self.play(Write(label_mp3))
        self.wait(2)

        SQUARE_COLOR = "#FF0000"

    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Real-World Application: Audio Compression"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Computers store these harmonic recipes instead of raw data.",
            "This \"shorthand\" allows for efficient digital audio compression.",
            "Fourier series turn complex sounds into simple, manageable lists."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lecture lines
        c1 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for recipe
        c2 = "#00FF00"  # Green for reconstruction
        c3 = "#FFFFFF"  # White for labels

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))

        # Recipe List: b1, b3, b5, b7, b9
        recipe_title = Text("Recipe [bn]", font_size=24, color=c1)
        # Position per Issue 40: B1
        self.place_at_grid(recipe_title, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
